parts.name: Stainless body
parts.desc: Flat stainless exterior panels create the truck’s distinctive planes and edges. The visible skin is only one part of the vehicle structure; the illustration should not be read as a crash-load or repair diagram.
parts.how: Stainless needs its own cleaning routine. Follow the manual for removing deposits and choosing products; paint-care advice does not automatically transfer.
facts: Stainless is not maintenance-free
Illustration is not a structural repair guide

parts.name: Glass & visibility
parts.desc: The glass roof and large windshield define the cabin. Laminated glass uses bonded layers to change how a pane behaves under impact and to reduce sound transmission.
parts.how: The view from the driver’s seat depends on mirrors, pillars, seating position and cameras together. Inspect the actual truck when judging sightlines; a 3D model cannot represent optical distortion or every blind spot.
facts: Glass remains breakable
Use actual sightlines when manoeuvring

parts.name: Light bar & lighting
parts.desc: The slim front light bar is a visual signature, while road lighting serves the practical job of making the route and the truck visible. Aesthetic light strips and headlamp functions are different things.
parts.how: Off-road lighting accessories have separate fitment and usage requirements. The model depicts a simplified lighting arrangement, not beam patterns or illumination distances.
facts: Model lighting is illustrative
Accessory availability varies

parts.name: Wheels & tyres
parts.kicker: The only contact with the road.
parts.desc: Tyres connect acceleration, braking and steering to the ground. Their size, construction, pressure and tread affect ride, noise, efficiency and load capacity.
parts.how: Use the pressures and fitments specified for the actual vehicle and task. Towing requirements can differ from ordinary loading instructions; changing tyres can change which limits apply.
facts: Wheel choice affects efficiency
Verify towing tyre guidance separately

parts.name: Braking & regeneration
parts.desc: The motors can turn motion back into electrical energy during deceleration. Friction brakes provide stopping force through pads and discs. They complement each other.
parts.how: Regenerative braking can be limited by battery conditions. Trailer braking and calibration add another system when towing; do not treat an energy-recovery graphic as a brake-capability test.
facts: Regeneration is not always fully available
Trailer braking requires its own setup

parts.name: Cabin & seating
parts.desc: A wide cabin and flat surfaces create a deliberately simple interior. Seat and trim equipment varies with the build and configuration.
parts.how: Look beyond screen size: seating position, rear-seat access, storage and visibility matter in daily use. Historical photos here show a particular truck, not a promise of current standard equipment.
facts: Photos retain their original vehicle context
Check equipment in the local configurator

parts.name: Screens & software
parts.desc: The central display brings vehicle settings, navigation, charging information and entertainment together. The availability of a rear display depends on the configuration.
parts.how: Software can change menus and features over time. Use the truck’s own settings and release notes when identifying what is installed; a photographed screen is a moment in time.
facts: Front and rear equipment can differ by trim
Software eligibility is vehicle-specific

parts.name: High-voltage battery
parts.kicker: The energy store under the cabin.
parts.desc: The traction battery stores energy for driving and other high-power functions. Cells, cooling, electronics and protective structure work as one managed system.
parts.how: An architecture class is not a universal nominal voltage, and an advertised pack size is not automatically usable energy. Our tools ask for assumptions instead of deriving a precise pack capacity from a trim badge.
facts: Energy is measured in kWh; power in kW
Temperature and charge level affect performance

parts.name: Rear drive unit
parts.desc: A drive unit combines electric motor hardware with reduction gearing and control electronics. Cybertruck configurations use different motor arrangements.
parts.how: The hidden components shown here explain packaging and energy flow. Their count, shape and location are simplified and do not identify a specific production drive-unit assembly.
facts: Current comparison trims use all-wheel drive
Illustrative geometry is not a parts catalogue

parts.name: Front drive unit
parts.desc: An electric drive at the front axle lets an all-wheel-drive system distribute propulsion between front and rear. Control software coordinates the available torque.
parts.how: The illustration shows the idea of an additional driven axle; it does not reveal the exact motor topology, output or calibration fitted to every Cybertruck.
facts: AWD describes driven axles, not identical motors
Output and equipment depend on configuration

parts.name: Power electronics
parts.kicker: The bridge between battery and motor.
parts.desc: Power electronics control the electrical supply to a traction motor. By changing current and frequency, the system controls torque and speed.
parts.how: During regeneration, electrical energy flows back toward the battery. Electronics, cooling and the battery’s charge-acceptance limits shape how much can be recovered.
facts: Electrical control changes motor behaviour
Power electronics need thermal management

parts.name: 48V architecture
parts.desc: Cybertruck uses a 48V lithium-ion low-voltage system for functions beyond propulsion. It is separate from the high-voltage traction battery.
parts.how: For a given electrical power, higher voltage permits lower current. That can reduce conductor requirements, but it does not make vehicle circuits safe to handle. Use the correct documentation and service equipment.
facts: 48V is not the traction-pack voltage
Do not assume conventional 12V accessories are compatible

parts.name: Steer-by-wire & rear steering
parts.kicker: A big truck that changes direction differently.
parts.desc: Electronic steering control replaces the conventional mechanical steering-shaft connection described in Tesla’s architecture material. Rear-wheel steering contributes to manoeuvrability.
parts.how: The controller can vary steering response with conditions rather than use one fixed relationship between steering-wheel movement and road-wheel angle. The simplified model is not a simulation of that control system.
facts: Steering response changes with operating conditions
Rear steering does not remove the need to check clearance

parts.name: Cargo bed & tonneau
parts.kicker: An open workspace. A covered vault.
parts.desc: The bed can carry bulky gear, while a tonneau cover, where fitted, provides enclosed storage. Not every build includes the same cover, rails or under-bed compartment.
parts.how: Check actual dimensions, equipment and loading instructions. Space and carrying weight are different limits; an item fitting inside does not mean the vehicle can carry its mass.
facts: Cover and storage equipment vary
Cargo must remain within the actual load limits

parts.name: Front storage
parts.desc: The front storage compartment adds another place to keep items separate from the passenger space and truck bed. The powered closure and its controls are part of the vehicle’s operating system.
parts.how: Use the manual when opening, loading or closing it, and follow the actual compartment limits. The model only shows approximate packaging.
facts: Use compartment-specific loading guidance
Keep closure areas clear

parts.name: Suspension & ride height
parts.desc: Cybertruck builds can use coil springs or adaptive air suspension. Adjustable ride height should not be assumed from the name alone.
parts.how: The manual explains how to identify the fitted system: ride-height controls indicate adaptive air suspension. Air-equipped trucks can change height for access or terrain, subject to operating limits.
facts: Check the installed suspension type
Extract Mode clearance is not a normal driving setting

parts.name: Charging hardware
parts.desc: The charge port sits above the driver-side rear wheel. AC charging and DC fast charging use different electrical paths and power limits.
parts.how: A published DC peak is a maximum under suitable conditions, not a full-session average. Starting charge, battery temperature and charging hardware affect the session. See the named reference curve below.
facts: Prepare the vehicle for the intended charging stop
Charging hardware and conditions matter

parts.name: Cameras & assistance
parts.desc: Cameras support the view around the vehicle and eligible driver-assistance functions. A camera’s presence does not prove that every software feature is enabled.
parts.how: Features depend on configuration, software and region. Full Self-Driving (Supervised) requires an attentive driver; the equipment shown here is not evidence of unsupervised driving capability.
facts: Check actual feature eligibility
Driver assistance requires supervision

parts.name: Climate & thermal management
parts.kicker: Comfort and battery conditions are connected.
parts.desc: Cabin heating, cooling and the battery’s thermal needs all draw on vehicle energy. Thermal management moves heat where it is needed or removes it.
parts.how: Preconditioning can change what happens at a charging stop, but weather and starting conditions still matter. A fixed charging-time claim cannot capture all of those differences.
facts: Climate use consumes energy
The charging curve depends on battery conditions
